Briefing for 20 November 2026

Short items for 20 November 2026. Sapaude writes them in its own words. Where a longer article exists, the link goes there. The publisher is Sapaude.

Everyday tool

Gemini can now operate apps on your Mac

The Gemini app for Mac can carry out multi-step tasks across local files, desktop apps and the web. It works in a separate background window, and you pick which apps it may use and approve its actions.

Source: Google

New model

GPT-Live-1.1 brings better voice chats to the API

OpenAI's updated full-duplex voice model pronounces and transcribes more accurately across languages and keeps a steadier accent. A new standby mode pauses inference while nobody is speaking.

Source: OpenAI

AI agents

ChatGPT tests its always-on dots with Plus users

OpenAI is trying its proactive dots agents with a small group of Plus subscribers and rolling them out to Business Standard. Users in the EU, the UK and Switzerland are excluded for now.

Source: 9to5Mac

Everyday tool

Pages, Numbers and Keynote open up to AI agents

Apple's iWork update adds an AI assistant in beta, US English only. On the Mac, MCP lets outside agents such as ChatGPT, Claude or local models edit documents, but only with a Creator Studio subscription.

Source: heise online

In the background

EU Commission confirms a cyberattack using an AI tool

The attack began on October 22 and took staff systems such as payroll offline for more than ten days. The Commission called it an AI-generated campaign; reports name the open-source hacking tool ARTEX.

Source: The Record

In the background

California proposes shutdown powers for risky AI

Governor Newsom's office released recommendations for mandatory safety standards, ongoing third-party oversight and emergency shutdown authority. These are proposals for legislation, not yet law.

Source: Governor of California

In the background

ECHR bars a lawyer over unchecked AI citations

The court's president excluded a lawyer from cases before the court for two years after a brief cited rulings that do not exist. The ban covers only the ECHR, and readmission remains possible.

Source: beck-aktuell

In the background

Report: Nvidia in talks to buy diffusion startup Inception

According to The Information, Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire Inception for more than $500 million. The startup builds diffusion language models that generate text in parallel instead of token by token.

Source: The Information

Be brave. Get smart.
